messages.subject: problem matching signature with .jcall for generic arrays
messages.subject_clean: problem matching signature with .jcall for generic arrays
messages.body_plain:
A user wanted to add a chart to a spreadsheet using the xlsx package. 
I've been stuck on this for a few hours now to pass the right arguments 
to a java method.

I'm trying to call the method:
http://poi.apache.org/apidocs/org/apache/poi/ss/usermodel/charts/DataSources.html#fromArray(T[])

>  jX <- .jcall('org.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.DataSources',
+          "Lorg.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.ChartDataSource;",
+          "fromArray",
+          .jarray(c(0,1,2,3)))
Error in .jcall("org.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.DataSources", 
"Lorg.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.ChartDataSource;",  :
   method fromArray with signature 
([D)Lorg.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.ChartDataSource; not found

I can see that I don't match the argument, I need an Object[].  I tried to 
use a .jcast, but it did not work either.

To reproduce the error:
library(xlsx)
jX <- .jcall('org.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.DataSources',
          "Lorg.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.ChartDataSource;",
          "fromArray",
          .jarray(c(0,1,2,3)))

Thank you for any suggestions,
Adrian

messages.body_plain:
On Dec 7, 2015, at 12:23 PM, Adrian Dragulescu <adrian_d at eskimo.com> wrote:

> 
> A user wanted to add a chart to a spreadsheet using the xlsx package. I've been stuck on this for a few hours now to pass the right arguments to a java method.
> 
> I'm trying to call the method:
> http://poi.apache.org/apidocs/org/apache/poi/ss/usermodel/charts/DataSources.html#fromArray(T[])
> 
>> jX <- .jcall('org.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.DataSources',
> +          "Lorg.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.ChartDataSource;",
> +          "fromArray",
> +          .jarray(c(0,1,2,3)))
> Error in .jcall("org.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.DataSources", "Lorg.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.ChartDataSource;",  :
>  method fromArray with signature ([D)Lorg.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.ChartDataSource; not found
> 


Lorg.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.ChartDataSource;
is not valid - Java uses / instead of . in actual names

so what you can use is

.jcall("org.apache.poi.ss.usermodel.charts.DataSources",
  "Lorg/apache/poi/ss/usermodel/charts/ChartDataSource;",
  "fromArray",
  .jcast(.jarray(c(0,1,2,3)),"[Ljava/lang/Object;"))

However, I don't know if arrays of unboxed types are supported by the code you're using. If not, you'll have to create boxed types.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: R server taking up high CPU on killing eval
messages.subject_clean: R server taking up high CPU on killing eval
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I have been working on the Rserve client for Java for sometime now. Some operations i do take a really long time and I wanted to kill them mid-way. After minimal research i came across the following method to do the same.
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/27066588/rserve-server-how-to-terminate-a-blocking-instance-eval-taking-forever/27144407?noredirect=1#comment56007066_27144407

My problem is as discussed on the thread.
I have Rserver running on a linux machine and i connect to that server using windows. Several connections could be made at a time from different client machines. On killing an eval, Rserve CPU utiliization on the server goes up and it doesnt allow any further connections. 
This happens after command to kill the targeted instance evals successfully and  returns.
At first i was using a global reference to the RserverConnection() and then i used a local variable as given in the above example. (See the comments on the above thread).The problem was solved, but when i try to make a connection at the exact time when someone is trying to kill another instance , Rserve freezes and doesnt allow that connection or any other afterwards.
I then tried to kill the eval using a system command with the targeted pid (I send commands to the server using ssh in java from the client). The problem still comes up but i cannot pin point the exact point. It happens on random when multiple clients are connected to the Rserve and someone requests a cancel. 
Do you have any idea why this might be happening and is there a neater way to kill an ongoing eval, a way  which doesnt freeze the Rserve?
Thanks and Regards,
Mohamed Raiyan

> 
> My problem is as discussed on the thread.
> 
> I have Rserver running on a linux machine and i connect to that server using windows. Several connections could be made at a time from different client machines.
>  
> On killing an eval, Rserve CPU utiliization on the server goes up and it doesnt allow any further connections. 
> 
> This happens after command to kill the targeted instance evals successfully and  returns.
> 
> At first i was using a global reference to the RserverConnection() and then i used a local variable as given in the above example. (See the comments on the above thread).
> The problem was solved, but when i try to make a connection at the exact time when someone is trying to kill another instance , Rserve freezes and doesnt allow that connection or any other afterwards.
> 
> I then tried to kill the eval using a system command with the targeted pid (I send commands to the server using ssh in java from the client). The problem still comes up but i cannot pin point the exact point. It happens on random when multiple clients are connected to the Rserve and someone requests a cancel. 
> 
> Do you have any idea why this might be happening and is there a neater way to kill an ongoing eval, a way  which doesnt freeze the Rserve?
> 

The client Rserve session are completely independent of the server, so it seems as if you're issuing signal to the wrong process. Another pointer may be that if you're using some common resource in your client sessions that can freezes your code across any connection (e.g. if you load a pre-load some packages or code) - but that's independent of Rserve.

So essentially we'll need the complete code for the minimal example to reproduce since this is likely something related to exactly what you're doing as opposed to Rserve itself.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I need some help using .jcall.  So far I have not found any good complicated examples on the web.  Can anyone point me to any?  Thank you.

I wish to call the following Java routine:

public static String[][] annotate (String[][] data, String build, Catalog[] catalogs, String[][] fields)

My questions are: how do I create a two dimensional java array?  I can’t use a matrix because the usb arrays do not have equal lengths.

My attempts, successes, and failures are below.  Sample code, pointers to sample code, pointers to how to search the archives, pointers to the place in the archives where this has been discussed 10^5 times before all greatly appreciated.

> control = bior.control()
> catalogs <- c()
> for (i in 1:length(control$catalogs$name)) {
+ catalogs <- c(catalogs, .jnew ("edu/mayo/bior/util/Catalog", control$catalogs$name[i],
+ control$catalogs$path[i], control$catalogs$overlap[i]))
+ }
> catalogs <- .jarray(catalogs, contents.class = "edu/mayo/bior/util/Catalog")
> catalogs
[1] "Java-Array-Object[Ledu/mayo/bior/util/Catalog;:[Ledu.mayo.bior.util.Catalog;@6526804e"

> fields <- c()
> theNames <- names(control$fields)
> for (i in 1:length(theNames)) {
+ fields <- c(fields, .jarray(c(theNames[i], control$fields[[i]]), contents.class = "java/lang/String"))
+ }
> fields <- .jarray(fields, contents.class = "[java/lang/String")
Error in .jarray(fields, contents.class = "[java/lang/String") :
  Cannot find class [java/lang/String.
> fields <- c()
> theNames <- names(control$fields)
> for (i in 1:length(theNames)) {
+ fields <- c(fields, .jarray(c(theNames[i], control$fields[[i]]), contents.class = "java/lang/String"))
+ }
> fields <- .jarray(fields, contents.class = "java/lang/String")
> fields
[1] "Java-Array-Object[Ljava/lang/String;:[Ljava.lang.String;@20d2906a”

> data <- c(.jarray(c("ted", "bike"), contents.class = "java/lang/String"), .jarray(c("mike", "ike"), contents.class = "java/lang/String"))
> data <- .jarray(data, contents.class = "java/lang/String")

[1] "Java-Array-Object[Ljava/lang/String;:[Ljava.lang.String;@77df38fd”

> output <- .jcall (control$target, "[[Ljava/lang/String;", "annotate", data, control$build, catalogs, fields)
Error in .jcall(control$target, "[[Ljava/lang/String;", "annotate", data,  :
  method annotate with signature ([Ljava/lang/String;Ljava/lang/String;[Ledu/mayo/bior/util/Catalog;[Ljava/lang/String;)[[Ljava/lang/String; not found

messages.subject: Re: Using JGR with Apple OS after Mavericks 10.9.5
messages.subject_clean: Using JGR with Apple OS after Mavericks 10.9.5
messages.body_plain:
How are you starting it? Have you installed Oracle Java + working rJava?

First, you should test form R directly with

library(JGR)
JGR()

That should start JGR. If not, you should see some errors that will point you in the right direction. Note that in El Capitan you will have to use rJava 0.9-8 due to a combination of bugs in Oracle Java and OS X. That means you'll need Xcode command line tools and use something like in R (not RStudio!):
install.packages("rJava",,"http://rforge.net")

If you have any specific questions, please post the exact error and details about your setup.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: rJava, segfaults on EC2 computers
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'd like to clarify that I'm emailing this list only because the
segfaults happen during rJava calls. The real reason could well be
elsewhere(RHIPE).

I've started an Elastic MapReduce cluster using AMI 3.3.2, c3.2xlarge nodes .

R is see below and rJava is "0.9-7" and Sun's java is
java version "1.7.0_71"
Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.7.0_71-b14)
Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 24.71-b01, mixed mode)

When I've started RHIPE, which makes extensive use of rJava, not
immediately, but sometime into the session, calling an rJava commands
results in


Error in .jcall("RJavaTools", "Ljava/lang/Object;", "invokeMethod", cl,  :
  ignoring SIGPIPE signal
> Warning: stack imbalance in '.External', 86 then -1
Warning: stack imbalance in '<-', 84 then -3
Warning: stack imbalance in 'if', 82 then -5
Error in .jcall("RJavaTools", "Ljava/lang/Object;", "invokeMethod", cl,  :

My question: has there been any issues running rJava on EC2 instances?
Is there something I can do debug this e..g track the culprit etc?

Cheers
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: rJava, segfaults on EC2 computers
messages.body_plain:
Saptarshi,

the issue seems related to the SIGPIPE error - apparently this happens somewhere deep inside where the error wreaks havoc. This typically means that you're closing some pipe (e.g. stdout/err or some direct socket) and then write to it (either intentionally or inadvertently). When using R with any native code you have to be very careful about pipes/sockets since R treats writing to a closed pipe as a bad error (and it's *anyone* writing to a closed socket, not just R itself). I don't think it has anything with EC2 but rather the exact sequence of events and code involved. From rJava's point of view I'd be interested which call exactly you get that error from, i.e. a backtrace from the C code would be very valuable here.

Thanks,
Simon
